requirements.evidence: Data model matches the contract: entities_slug_unique (create_entities_table.php:17), entity_memberships_entity_user_unique and storedAs owner_seq + entity_memberships_one_owner (create_entity_memberships_table.php:20-22). Policies match the rules (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:31-46 blocks owner deletion, allows self-removal). Middleware dispatch 0/1/>1 + 403 (ResolveCurrentEntity.php:37-76); /home dispatch (routes/web.php:16-33); pick route 403 + audit log + redirect (routes/web.php:51-66); CreateEntity calls uniqueSlug() on each attempt and retries on unique violation (CreateEntity.php:115-138); dashboard authorizes view (Dashboard.php:17); switcher markup with data-current="1" and is-link/is-light; navbar link only when memberships > 1; lang keys in both locales. Gaps: soft-deleted entity in the 1-membership branch yields `$entity->id` on null (ResolveCurrentEntity.php:66-68, routes/web.php:26-27), and a stale session entity aborts 403 without clearing the session.

conventions.evidence: No Action class for the entity-creation domain write: the transaction lives in the Livewire component (CreateEntity.php:120-132) despite 'Domain writes go through app/Actions/*'. The pick route authorizes with an inline membershipFor check + abort(403) (routes/web.php:54-56) instead of going through EntityPolicy. Business logic sits in route closures (routes/web.php:16-33, 41-66). The diff has no tests, which breaks the mandatory TDD convention. On the positive side, it uses #[Validate] + validate(), sets $fillable on both models, registers the persistent middleware, uses existing Blade components (x-form-field, x-button) and updates docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md.

security.evidence: CreateEntity validates name and authorizes create (CreateEntity.php:103,108-110); the creator role is hard-coded Owner with auth()->id() (CreateEntity.php:126-129); Dashboard authorizes view in mount (Dashboard.php:17); ResolveCurrentEntity is added via Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware (AppServiceProvider.php:542-544); all output uses {{ }}. Small gaps: pick authorization skips the policy layer (routes/web.php:54), and the dashboard does not reconcile the session tenant with the route entity, so the in-request tenant context can point at a different entity than the one shown.

tests.evidence: The diff adds no test files at all: nothing for the migrations/one-owner invariant, the policies, the middleware, /home dispatch, pick, onboarding (including the required unauthorized and tamper tests for CreateEntity::submit), dashboard 403 or the switcher markup.

simplicity.evidence: The code is mostly lean. However, the 0/1/>1 dispatch is duplicated between ResolveCurrentEntity.php:59-76 and routes/web.php:19-32, and the same attribute and container setup is repeated twice in the middleware (lines 52-54 and 69-71). isUniqueViolation does broad string matching (CreateEntity.php:169-177).

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small and the models use PHPDoc generics like their siblings. There are a few leftovers: empty generator constructors in the policies (EntityPolicy.php:14-17) and an unneeded `?? config('app.name')` fallback on a non-null name (Dashboard.php:213). The route closures make routes/web.php heavier.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. There is no members/settings page, no locale middleware and no navbar redesign; docs and changelog edits are the ones the task requires.

issues.explanation: No tests ship with any of the new behaviour, which violates the mandatory TDD convention and the Livewire definition of done (unauthorized and tamper tests).
Entity creation is a domain write and should go through an app/Actions class (for example CreateEntity), not run inline in the Livewire component.
The pick route authorizes with an inline membership check instead of the EntityPolicy (`can:view,entity` or Gate/authorize).
If the single membership's entity is soft-deleted, `$membership->entity` is null and `->id` raises an error instead of handling the case.
A session pointing to an entity the user left or that was deleted aborts 403 on every request and is never cleared, so the user stays stuck until they pick again.
The membership dispatch logic is duplicated from the middleware, and the route closures hold logic that would be clearer in a controller.
The `?? config('app.name')` fallback is dead code because the entity name is required.
Empty generator constructors are leftover boilerplate.

review.summary: The change implements the entities data model with a DB-enforced one-owner invariant, the policies, the tenant middleware, /home dispatch, onboarding with slug-collision retry, the pick route, the dashboard, the switcher and the navbar entry, and updates the docs. Functionally it covers the task well and stays in scope. It ships with no tests at all, and the entity-creation domain write bypasses the project's Actions convention, so it needs substantial rework before merging.
